analyst_view.overall: Third-placed Inter (29 points, three behind leaders Lazio) host Genoa (10th, 16 points, four wins in five under Daniele De Rossi) on Saturday evening; the numbers make Inter clear favourites. Cristian Chivu's side drew 4-4 at Atalanta and play Stuttgart in the Champions League at San Siro tonight (25 November), so they get three days before Genoa. Calhanoglu (hamstring), Zielinski and Bonny are out, and the numbers now count all three (about -16% on Inter's goals), so I no longer size them for goals; Lautaro is back from his muscle injury and is being eased in, with Internews24 and Gazzetta reporting the Genoa game as the target for his return to the starting XI. Genoa lost forward Lorenzo Colombo to a torn cruciate ligament (counted by the numbers), centre-back Ostigard spent a night in hospital with flu but is recovering, and Vitinha or Osmajic should lead the line. No referee is named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, 1.9 for Inter. My earlier lean lower was for Calhanoglu, Zielinski and Bonny being out, but the numbers now take them off (about -16% on Inter's goals), and Lautaro returning to the XI roughly offsets the three-day turnaround after Stuttgart. Colombo's loss for Genoa is also counted, so I move to the numbers at about 2.7.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners, 6.6 for Inter, already raised for Inter's busy recent corner count (+5.4%) and lowered for Genoa's (-4.3%). Inter's wing-backs Dimarco and Spence or Augusto drive most of their corners whoever plays in midfield, and Genoa defend in a back three, so nothing new points either way and I stay at about 9.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.1 cards, already lowered because both sides have been booked less than usual lately (about -9% each). No referee is named yet, Genoa are clear of the relegation zone and this is no derby, so I see no reason for a heated game and stay at 3.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.1 shots, already lifted for Inter's heavy recent shooting (+15.8%). The missing players only move the goals, not the shots, so I still trim a little to about 29.2: without Calhanoglu and Zielinski Inter lose their main long-range shooters, Sucic is expected in the playmaker role, and some rotation is likely three days after Stuttgart. The lean stays small because Lautaro, Thuram and Pio Esposito are all available.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.4 shots on target, 6.6 for Inter, already raised for their recent accuracy (+5.8%). For the same reasons as shots (Calhanoglu and Zielinski out, a three-day turnaround after a Champions League game) I go a little lower to about 9.1. Genoa's attack without Colombo, who was mostly a part-time starter, changes little.
